title: SOV-B1: Sovereign Territory Battery — Charter Supremacy, Treaty Borders, Sovereign Budget, and No-Self-Pardon Containment on a Zero-Lineage LLM Consensus Cluster (6/11 Metrics Pass, 3 Deviations Journaled and Remediated Same Day)
description:
SQUIRL OS RESEARCH DISCLOSURE — READ FIRST: AI-assisted, receipt-first research program (open-book doctrine: audit-and-correction, versioned amendments, append-only public ledger). Errors are disclosed, not erased. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. Not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All payloads synthetic.

SOV-B1 — Sovereign Territory Battery: charter supremacy, treaty-based borders, sovereign budget, and no-self-pardon containment on a zero-lineage LLM consensus cluster (CONCLAVE-3). SQUIRL OS governs LLM-proposed changes with deterministic consensus. SOV-B1 tests the sovereignty stack above that consensus: an immutable charter hashed at every epoch boundary, cross-territory imports gated by treaty policy, a sovereign treasury that holds all writes when exhausted, and the requirement that every privileged action (node restore, rogue disarm, held-crossing release, charter amendment) carry an explicit sovereign token. Executed under a locked preregistration across epochs EPOCH-0002 through EPOCH-0010 on a fresh zero-lineage box.

Results (receipted): Charter invariance 9/9 epochs byte-identical; node-initiated charter amendments 100% blocked and parked pending sovereign approval (no self-amendment); budget hold 100% under exhaustion with zero unauthorized spend; sovereign continuity 100% (charter, sentinel, and border operations continued while the treasury was drained); liveness recovery 12/12 clean crossings in a fresh epoch. Union-of-holds stress: with a drifted node, a rogue-armed node, a drained treasury, and a rogue-source foreign import active simultaneously, the clean in-flight crossing survived untouched and recovered to quorum after the sovereign restore sequence, while new writes were held and the rogue import was quarantined at the border.

Honest deviations (journaled verbatim, never patched in-run; 3 of 11 preregistered metrics failed and are attributed to these): (1) SOV-DEV-1: disarmRogueNode lacked the sovereign token guard its sibling functions enforce — a rogue node self-disarmed (1/4 self-pardon attempts succeeded). (2) SOV-DEV-2: the integrity sentinel evaluated historical journal rows against current state, producing false violations from true records (8 of 10 final flags). (3) SOV-DEV-3: the border checked treaty status but not source status — an active treaty admitted a rogue-source import into consensus space (contained: the proposal never received a vote or quorum).

Same-day remediation (owner-approved, deployed, and re-verified on the box): SIP-1 mirrored the sovereign token guard onto disarmRogueNode (verified: tokenless self-disarm now refused 403, fail-closed). SIP-2 scoped the sentinel's evaluation to epoch context and made the sovereign budget ledger append-only per operation with an explicit exhaustion flag, eliminating the lifecycle false-positive class and making exhaustion history reconstructable for future epochs (the pre-fix overwrite means historical exhaustion context survives only in the sealed transcript and this report — accurately flagged, not silently resolved). SIP-3 added a border source-status gate: rogue or drifted sources are quarantined regardless of treaty state (verified: rogue-source import quarantined under an active admitting treaty; clean imports still admitted — no over-blocking).
